deckTitle: Pattern C — Dynamic Hybrid: One Control Plane, Pooled & Sovereign Tiers, Live Upgrades
deckSubtitle: Tenant-aware hub routing Standard to a shared pool and Enterprise over Private Service Connect to CMEK spokes, with 0-dropped-turn upgrades
tldr: Tiered SaaS needs Pattern A economics for Standard and Pattern B sovereignty for Enterprise — Pattern C serves both behind one SaaS URL.
Unified Hybrid Control Hub (cymbal-hybrid-hub-prod): Cloud Armor/IAP, Cloud Run Router, Firestore Route Table, Cross-Project ARD Federated GEAP Registry.
RetailStream (Standard) runs in the Shared Pooled Runtime at a 4,000 thinking cap; FinVault (Enterprise) is reached over PSC at psc://10.10.0.50.
3-Phase engine (SHADOW_SYNC → ATOMIC_CUTOVER → DRAIN_AND_VERIFY) promotes RetailStream to its own CMEK PSC spoke on the same live session.
4.5 suite verifies 4/4 PASS: 0 ms replication lag, 0 dropped sessions, 8,000 budget unclamped, rs-agent-cmek bound, zero global state bleed.

sections.heading: Why Tiered SaaS Needs Both Pooled and Sovereign
bullets: RetailStream Corp: Microsoft Entra ID, shared Diagnostic Agent only, 4,000 thinking cap, shared AlloyDB RLS, SharePoint/ServiceNow via inline 3LO.
FinVault Bank: Google Workspace OIDC, private Agent Alpha (Claude Sonnet), 8,000 budget, CMEK AlloyDB in a VPC-SC spoke, Workspace/Jira via 3LO.
Neither pure pattern fits both rows; two disconnected stacks double the control plane and turn tier upgrades into maintenance windows.
4.4 triage: if you sell Standard on shared infra plus Enterprise with dedicated data spokes and custom agents, deploy Pattern C.

sections.heading: Hybrid Hub-and-Spoke Control Plane
bullets: Single project cymbal-hybrid-hub-prod owns the public URL, External Application Load Balancer, Cloud Armor and IAP for both tiers.
Cloud Run Router resolves the Hop 1 verified tenant_id against the Firestore Route Table: PATTERN_C_HYBRID_POOL or PATTERN_C_HYBRID_PSC_SPOKE.
Standard route pool://cymbal-shared-pooled-runtime-v2; Enterprise route psc://10.10.0.50/.../finvault-agent-spoke-psc.
PSC producer ServiceAttachment uses ACCEPT_MANUAL with a hub-only accept list; spokes reuse 10.40.0.0/20 and cannot reach back into the hub.
Cross-Project ARD Federated GEAP Registry surfaces Agent Alpha to FinVault while returning 403 Forbidden to RetailStream.

sections.heading: The 5-Hop Chain in Pattern C
bullets: Hop 1 strips forged X-Tenant-ID headers, verifies IdP JWT, mints RFC 8693 OBO + DPoP context — the only input to routing.
Hop 2 federates spoke agent cards into the hub PDP and prunes tools via ADK 2.0 before_agent_callback.
Hop 3 enforces 4,000 vs 8,000 budgets and Redis bulkheads from an instance-scoped tenant_profiles dict — never global TENANT_PROFILES.
Hop 4 runs Shared Model Armor Multi-Tenant Prompt & SDP in the pool and Spoke Model Armor Dedicated Spoke DLP & NLC in each spoke.
Hop 5 binds SET LOCAL app.current_tenant for AlloyDB RLS, brokers 2LO/3LO tokens, and emits OTel audit traces to BigQuery.

sections.heading: Zero-Downtime Live Tier Upgrade (Standard → Enterprise)
bullets: TEST 1A/1B: RetailStream clamped to 4,000 in the pool; FinVault gets 8,000 over PSC on sess-fv-hybrid-01.
SHADOW_SYNC: Terraform provisions cymbal-retailstream-spoke-prod, CMEK key and PSC attachment; RLS rows replicate to 0 ms lag.
ATOMIC_CUTOVER: one replace() profile write flips tier, 8,000 budget, redis_rpm_limit 600, CMEK and route to psc://10.10.0.51.
DRAIN_AND_VERIFY: in-flight pooled turns finish; dropped_sessions == 0; status MIGRATION_COMPLETE.
TEST 3: same sess-rs-live-upgrade-01 and DPoP key now ENTERPRISE, unclamped 8,000, rs-agent-cmek bound.

sections.heading: Product Collaboration, Terraform Blueprint & Codelab
bullets: 4.4 aligned Cross-Project Registry, PSC Spoke Bridge and Live Tier Migration with product engineering plus a GA Field Enablement Playbook.
4.6 main.tf: hub VPC/subnet 10.10.0.0/20, spoke PSC NAT subnet 10.40.240.0/24, service attachment, 10.10.0.50 consumer endpoint.
90-minute L400 Master Codelab: router, PSC wiring, SHADOW_SYNC + ATOMIC_CUTOVER, DRAIN_AND_VERIFY session continuity.
go/demos slug geap-multi-tenant-pattern-c-hybrid with a 5-minute video script ending on ALL 4 PATTERN C TESTS PASSED.

sections.heading: FinOps & SLA Outcomes
bullets: Pooled tier keeps up to 90% COGS savings from shared ContextCacheConfig; enterprise spokes get dedicated quotas with zero noisy neighbours.
Budgets, rate limits and CMEK live in one instance-scoped profile and flip atomically — no half-migrated state.
Unidirectional PSC limits blast radius: the hub initiates, the spoke never connects back.
Standard → Enterprise becomes a same-day product action with no URL change and no re-authentication.

diagrams.title: Pattern C: Dynamic Hybrid Hub-and-Spoke, Private Service Connect & Live Tier Migration
talkingPoints: Start at the actor: Standard & Enterprise Single Unified SaaS URL — one hostname for both tiers, step 1 Request in, step 7 Response out.
Routing hub: Cloud Armor & IAP + OBO/DPoP, Cross-Project ARD Federated GEAP Registry, Firestore Route Table, ALB, Cloud Run Router.
Governance hub: 3-Phase Zero-Downtime Tier Migration Engine — SHADOW_SYNC (0ms Lag Copy), ATOMIC_CUTOVER, DRAIN_AND_VERIFY (4/4 PASS).
Trunk badge 3 'Route Standard to Pool or Enterprise via PSC' fans out; badge 7 'Seamless response (0 dropped sessions)' returns.
Left spoke: Shared Pooled Runtime with Gemini 2.5 Pro 4,000 Thinking Cap + Cache and Shared AlloyDB RLS that Streams State to PSC Spoke.
Right spoke: Dedicated Enterprise PSC Spokes, Unidirectional PSC Bridge, CMEK Spoke AlloyDB; dashed Live promotion: Pool -> PSC Spoke.

diagrams.title: Pattern C Demo Environment: Central Ingress Hub, Shared Pool & PSC Service Attachment Spokes
talkingPoints: One hub project (cymbal-hybrid-hub-prod, cymbal-hub-vpc / cymbal-hub-subnet) fronts both tiers behind a single Global ALB + Cloud Armor + IAP URL.
The Firestore routing table and cross-project GEAP registry decide per tenant: Standard → pool://cymbal-shared-pooled-runtime-v2, Enterprise → psc://.
Producer side lives in the tenant spoke: a 10.40.240.0/24 PSC NAT subnet plus finvault-agent-spoke-psc (ACCEPT_MANUAL, accept-list hub project = 10).
Consumer side lives in the hub: reserve psc-endpoint-finvault-ip (10.10.0.50) and bind psc-consumer-finvault to the spoke's ServiceAttachment URI.
PSC is NAT-based, so every spoke may reuse 10.40.0.0/20 with no CIDR overlap, and exposure is unidirectional — spokes cannot reach back into the hub VPC.
Step 7 closes the loop: run_tier_migration_suite.py verifies hybrid routing and the live tier upgrade locally before any customer traffic hits the demo.

diagrams.title: Zero-Downtime Tier Upgrade Test Sequence: SHADOW_SYNC → ATOMIC_CUTOVER → DRAIN_AND_VERIFY (4/4 PASS)
talkingPoints: run_tier_migration_suite.py drives PatternCHybridRouterAndMigrator through 4 assertions-backed tests; nothing mutates the global TENANT_PROFILES.
TEST 1A/1B fix the baseline: retailstream → PATTERN_C_HYBRID_POOL clamped to 4,000 tokens; finvault → PATTERN_C_HYBRID_PSC_SPOKE over psc:// with 8,000.
TEST 2 runs the 3-phase engine: SHADOW_SYNC (replication_lag_ms == 0, PSC_CONNECTION_ACCEPTED) → ATOMIC_CUTOVER → DRAIN_AND_VERIFY (dropped_sessions == 0).
The cutover flips routing_table['retailstream'] to tier ENTERPRISE, budget 8,000, target psc://10.10.0.51/... and state UPGRADED_ZERO_DOWNTIME_SPOKE.
TEST 3 reuses the same session_id (sess-rs-live-upgrade-01) and asserts PSC routing, thinking_budget_clamped is False, and rs-agent-cmek in cmek_key_uri.
Left spoke = the pooled source rows stream from; right spoke = cymbal-retailstream-spoke-prod, the CMEK target that status MIGRATION_COMPLETE confirms.

diagrams.title: Terraform Hybrid PSC Blueprint Resource Graph: Hub VPC → Consumer PSC Endpoint → Producer ServiceAttachment in Enterprise Spoke
talkingPoints: main.tf pins terraform >= 1.5.0 and hashicorp/google >= 5.30.0, then declares two provider aliases — google.hub and google.spoke — fed by five variables.
Hub side: google_compute_network.cymbal_hub_vpc (cymbal-hybrid-hub-vpc) and cymbal_hub_subnet at 10.10.0.0/20 with private Google access enabled.
Spoke side: enterprise_spoke_vpc, a 10.40.240.0/24 PRIVATE_SERVICE_CONNECT NAT subnet, and ${tenant}-agent-spoke-psc with ACCEPT_MANUAL and connection_limit 20.
The consumer bridge is two resources: google_compute_address.hub_psc_consumer_ip (10.10.0.50) and google_compute_forwarding_rule.hub_psc_consumer_endpoint.
Two outputs — psc_service_attachment_uri and hub_psc_consumer_ip — feed the 4.3 router's Firestore route table; those hub consumers are not resources here.
tfvars example targets cymbal-hybrid-hub-prod ↔ cymbal-finvault-silo-prod with finvault-spoke-ilb as target_service; README quickstart is init → plan → apply.

takeaways: Pattern C routes isolation instead of duplicating it: one control plane, one URL, two execution tiers.
Routing is keyed only on the Hop 1 cryptographic tenant_id — a client header can never claim Enterprise tier.
Instance-scoped profile mutation makes the live upgrade safe: zero global state bleed across tenants or test runs.
Private Service Connect removes CIDR overlap and VPC-peering limits while keeping spokes unidirectional and VPC-SC compatible.
The migration is measurable: 0 ms lag, 0 dropped sessions, same session id, 4/4 suite gates passing.
callToAction: Apply the 4.6 Terraform PSC blueprint, run the 4.5 zero-downtime upgrade suite, then continue to Workstream 5 for the decision guide and capstone.
